title.narrative: Integrated REDD+ Program Equateur II (PiREDD Equateur II)
Integrerat REDD+ Program Equateur II (PiREDD Equateur II)

description.narrative:
Sweden will finance the PIREDD project in Equateur Province as part of its broader support for the Democratic Republic of Congos (DRC) national strategy to reduce deforestation and forest degradation (REDD). Equateur is one of DRCs key forest provinces and forms part of the worlds second-largest rainforest. The province has an area of 104,000 km of which 87,000 km (84%) consists of forest. The forest in Equateur is of critical importance for the local, regional, and global climate since the forest influences rainfall patterns that are essential for agriculture, a primary source of livelihood for the Congolese population.
The national REDD fund (FONAREDD) was established by the DRC government under the leadership of CAFI to operationalize the REDD strategy, mobilize resources, and coordinate the implementation of various projects. CAFI (Central African Forest Initiative) is a fund aimed at reducing deforestation in Central Africa which, among others, is funded by Sidas regional strategy for Africa. This initiative therefore creates synergies between Sidas regional and bilateral development cooperation efforts.
The overarching goal of FONAREDD is sustainable forest management focusing on diversifying income sources for local populations to reduce their dependency on forest exploitation. The projects primary objectives are to: (i) reduce greenhouse gas emissions by preventing deforestation and forest degradation; (ii) promote sustainable livelihoods for local communities, especially Indigenous peoples; and (iii) ensure the inclusion of women and youth in decision-making on income generating activities and land tenure. The intervention includes six components: community governance, land rights, forestry, agriculture, energy, and family planning. Integrating these components ensures agricultural practices are sustained and that land conflicts between the Bantu and Indigenous populations are mitigated against even after the project comes to an end.
The project strengthens local institutions and civil society organizations to enhance forest management. Local development plans place responsibility and ownership in the hands of the communities living in and relying on the forest. Special emphasis is placed on involving indigenous peoples to ensure that alternative livelihoods funded by the project meet local needs and align with local markets.
The contribution will last for 4 years, from 2024-2028.

Sverige finansierar projektet PIREDD i provinsen Equateur som en del av sitt bredare stöd till Demokratiska Republiken Kongos (DRK) nationella strategi för att minska avskogning och degradering av skog (REDD+). Equateur är en av DRK:s viktigaste skogsprovinser och en del av världens näst största regnskog. Provinsen täcker 104 000 km², varav 87 000 km² (84 %) utgörs av skog som är avgörande för lokalt, regionalt och globalt klimat. Skogen påverkar nederbördsmönster och därmed jordbruket som är en central försörjningskälla för den kongolesiska befolkningen. Denna insatsen är därför ett viktigt bidrag till klimat och miljömålen i Sveriges strategi för utvecklingssamarbetet för DRK.
Den nationella REDD-fonden (FONAREDD) skapades av DRK:s regering under CAFI:s ledning för att operationalisera REDD+-strategin, mobilisera medel och samordna olika projekt. CAFI (Central African Forest Initiative) är en fond för att minska avskogningen i Centralafrika och finansieras bland annat av Sida genom den regionala Afrikastrategin. Insatsen skapar därför synergier mellan Sidas regionala och bilaterala arbete.
FONAREDD:s övergripande mål är en hållbar skogsförvaltning, med fokus på att diversifiera lokalbefolkningens inkomstkällor för att minska beroendet av skogen för överlevnad. Projektets huvudmål är att: i) minska växthusgasutsläpp genom att motverka avskogning och degradering, ii) främja hållbara försörjningsmöjligheter för lokalsamhällen, särskilt för ursprungsbefolkningar, och iii) säkerställa att kvinnor och ungdomar inkluderas i strategiska beslut om inkomstskapande aktiviteter och markägande. Genomförandet av insatsen omfattar sex områden: samhällsstyrning, markrättigheter, skogsbruk, jordbruk, energi och familjeplanering. Integreringen av dessa komponenter säkerställer hållbara jordbruksmetoder och minimerar markkonflikter mellan bantu och ursprungsbefolkningar.
Projektet stärker lokala institutioner och civilsamhällesorganisationer för att förbättra skogsförvaltningen. Lokala utvecklingsplaner lägger ansvar och ägande i händerna på de samhällen som lever i och av skogen. Särskild vikt läggs vid att involvera ursprungsbefolkningar för att säkerställa att alternativa försörjningsmöjligheter är anpassade till lokala behov och marknader. Lokala utvecklingskommittéer och andra offentliga strukturer säkerställer samhällsengagemang, med fokus på kvinnors deltagande i beslutsfattande och ekonomiska aktiviteter. Projektet kommer att pågå i 4 år (2024-2028).

Sweden will finance the PIREDD project in Equateur Province as part of its broader support for the Democratic Republic of Congo’s (DRC) national strategy to reduce deforestation and forest degradation (REDD+). Equateur is one of DRC’s key forest provinces and forms part of the world’s second-largest rainforest. The province has an area of 104,000 km² of which 87,000 km² (84%) consists of forest. The forest in Equateur is of critical importance for the local, regional, and global climate since the forest influences rainfall patterns that are essential for agriculture, a primary source of livelihood for the Congolese population.
The national REDD+ fund (FONAREDD) was established by the DRC government under the leadership of CAFI to operationalize the REDD+ strategy, mobilize resources, and coordinate the implementation of various projects. CAFI (Central African Forest Initiative) is a fund aimed at reducing deforestation in Central Africa which, among others, is funded by Sida’s regional strategy for Africa. This initiative therefore creates synergies between Sida’s regional and bilateral development cooperation efforts.
The overarching goal of FONAREDD is sustainable forest management focusing on diversifying income sources for local populations to reduce their dependency on forest exploitation. The project’s primary objectives are to: (i) reduce greenhouse gas emissions by preventing deforestation and forest degradation; (ii) promote sustainable livelihoods for local communities, especially Indigenous peoples; and (iii) ensure the inclusion of women and youth in decision-making on income generating activities and land tenure. The intervention includes six components: community governance, land rights, forestry, agriculture, energy, and family planning. Integrating these components ensures agricultural practices are sustained and that land conflicts between the Bantu and Indigenous populations are mitigated against even after the project comes to an end.
The project strengthens local institutions and civil society organizations to enhance forest management. Local development plans place responsibility and ownership in the hands of the communities living in and relying on the forest. Special emphasis is placed on involving indigenous peoples to ensure that alternative livelihoods funded by the project meet local needs and align with local markets. The contribution will last for 4 years, from 2024-2028.

The results of the project are as follows: :
Result 1: Strengthen Governance through capacity building of decentralized technical services (Ministries of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment) and the establishment of local community management structures represented, as appropriate, by Local Development Committees (CLD) and Farmers' Associations and Organizations (AP/OP) (Pillar: Governance).
Result 2: Reduce pressure on forests and respect the rights and land needs of local communities through optimized planning and land utilisation. (Pillar: Spatial planning).
Result 3: Forest carbon stocks and peatland areas are safeguarded through the promotion of community forestry (Pillar: Forestry)
Result 4: Non-itinerant agriculture is developed through sustainable models in savannah areas and in post-crop fallows to limit slash-and-burn agriculture in natural forests and increase the income of populations. (Pillar: Agriculture)
Result 5: To avoid cutting of the natural forest the production of wood energy is to made from sustainable sources of supply in woodlands established on the outskirts of large population centres, in savannahs and around homes in rural areas (Pillar: Energy)
Result 6: Local populations and indigenous peoples have access to information and services for maternal health including informed choice of contraception in order to reduce maternal mortality. (Pillar: Demography).
